prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- If you want convenience for shows, restaurants and shopping: stay at a hotel on/near 76 Country Boulevard or Branson Landing.  
- If you want space, a kitchen, privacy or lake access (best for families or groups): rent an Airbnb/cabin on or near Table Rock Lake or in the Ozarks.  
- If you want a true resort/luxury experience: book Big Cedar Lodge or Chateau on the Lake.

Why choose one over the other
- Hotel pros: daily housekeeping, on‑site front desk, pools/parking/amenities, easy walk or short drive to theaters and Branson Landing, predictable service. Better for short stays, couples who want convenience, and seniors.
- Hotel cons: less space and privacy, higher cost per person for groups, can be noisy if on the Strip.
- Airbnb/cabin pros: more bedrooms and living space, kitchen (save on meals), lakefront decks/hot tubs, better value for groups, very scenic/secluded options.
- Airbnb cons: variable quality between listings, cleaning/booking fees, no daily housekeeping, might be farther from show theaters unless you pick downtown/condo listings.

Where to stay (neighborhood guidance)
- Branson Landing / Downtown: best for restaurants, shopping, lakefront strolling and family-friendly shows. Hotels here are convenient for evenings.
- 76 Country Boulevard (the “Strip”): central for the major theaters, dinner shows and attractions (Titanic, Ripley’s, Adventure USA).
- Table Rock Lake / Indian Point / Hollister: best for boating, swimming, nature and big cabins with views — farther from the Strip but scenic.
- Branson West / near Silver Dollar City: convenient if Silver Dollar City is the main reason for your trip.

Specific recommended hotels (good for convenience and reliability)
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale, lakefront, spa, great for couples and special occasions.
- Big Cedar Lodge (near Branson, in Ridgedale) — resort cabins, fishing and outdoor activities, top‑tier resort experience.
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — excellent location on the Landing, walk to shops/restaurants, good mid‑upscale option.
- Radisson Hotel Branson (or similarly rated chain hotels downtown) — reliable amenities and central location.
- Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — uniquely run hotel/restaurant with high quality service (book early).
- Chain options for budgets/families: Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Best Western properties around Branson or Branson West.

What to look for in Airbnbs (types to search)
- Lakefront Table Rock cabins — choose private dock, boat parking if you plan to bring or rent a boat.
- Downtown/Branson Landing condos — walk to shows and restaurants, good if you want Airbnb space but hotel‑like walkability.
- Secluded Ozark cabins with hot tub/fire pit — great for couples and relaxation.
- Large multi‑bedroom homes near 76 Boulevard — ideal for families/groups who want to be close to theaters.

Booking tips
- Book early for summer, fall festival weekends and Christmas show season; Branson fills up fast.
- Compare total cost: cleaning fees, resort fees, parking and taxes can change the value equation.
- For Airbnbs: read recent reviews, check host cancellation policy and arrival logistics (keys/parking).
- For hotels: ask about shuttle service to theaters, resort fees, and whether breakfast is included.
- If you’ll see lots of shows, prioritize location over views to minimize driving/parking hassles.

Quick recommendations by trip type
- Romantic / luxury: Chateau on the Lake or a secluded lakefront cabin at Table Rock Lake.
- Family or multi‑family group: a large Airbnb cabin on the lake or Big Cedar Lodge cabins/resort units.
- Show/first‑time visitors who want easy access: Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing or a hotel on 76 Country Boulevard.
- Budget conscious: chain hotels a little off the Strip or an affordable multi‑bedroom Airbnb outside downtown.

If you want, tell me:
- your travel dates, group size, and priorities (shows vs. boating vs. hiking vs. relaxation), and I’ll suggest 3–5 specific properties or current listing types that would fit your needs.
